quote: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale: Meets the preferred position: Vendor IP indemnity covering Customer and Affiliates (20.1), plus breach of law, bodily injury/property damage, Customer Data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud (20.2); standard notice/cooperation/control procedure (20.4); procure-modify-replace-refund remedies (20.5); and Customer's indemnity narrowly limited to Customer-supplied material and Customer's violation of law (20.3). Indemnities also sit outside the liability cap as Excluded Claims.

quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
rationale: Preferred position met: Customer owns Customer Data and its own IP with no transfer to Vendor beyond a service-provision processing right (§14.1), Vendor assigns Deliverables (§14.2), embedded Vendor Technology carries the perpetual §13.2 licence (§14.3), and no joint ownership is created (§14.4).
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The cap is tied to "Fees", which is defined as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the mutual cap is illusory. We have changed the basis to the greater of all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and Order Forms in the preceding 12 months and USD 1,000,000; the Excluded Claims (indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) remain outside the cap.

ops.newText: shall not exceed the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000
ops.oldText: shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim

proposal.summary: Fix illusory cap basis: all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement, greater of 12 months' amounts or USD 1,000,000

quote: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
rationale: The cap is mutual and the carve-outs and damages exclusions are fully compliant (Excluded Claims cover confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement; Customer's payment obligation is not "damages"). However, the cap basis is illusory: "Fees" is defined as the Implementation Fee, a one-time USD 12,000 charge under the first Order Form (§§1.5, 1.6), so the aggregate cap for both parties is effectively USD 12,000 — far below the fallback of 12 months' fees and below the 6-month walk-away floor. Redline changes the basis to the greater of all amounts paid or payable in the preceding 12 months and USD 1,000,000.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
rationale: Preferred position met: Customer has a consent-free affiliate/successor assignment right; Vendor needs Customer's consent (reasonableness qualified) and may never assign to a Customer competitor; and §24.4 expressly denies Vendor any termination, suspension, repricing or acceleration right on Customer's change of control.

quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Customer; §12.3 expressly preserves our right to engage any supplier and §2.1 confirms Customer buys only what it orders. Preferred position met.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer; a 15% of annual Fees per-week charge is punitive and unbounded, so we have deleted it. If Vendor needs a late-payment remedy, we can accept simple interest at a commercially reasonable rate on undisputed overdue amounts.
proposal.summary: Delete the 15%-per-week liquidated damages payable by Customer for late payment

quote: If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages on Customer of 15% of annual Fees per week of late payment, with no cap — an uncapped penalty triggered by a minor administrative breach, which is walk-away territory under this rule. We have deleted it; ordinary interest on undisputed overdue amounts is the acceptable substitute.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

quote: Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes
rationale: Preferred position met: the grant expressly covers Affiliates and contractors, paid-up/embedded material is perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free with modification rights (§13.2), rights are transferable to an Affiliate or successor (§13.3), and revocation/suspension is limited to material uncured breach after notice and cure.

quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory.
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds Customer; §12.3 affirmatively confirms Customer's freedom to operate. The only competitive restriction (§12.4) binds Vendor, which benefits us and is not flagged.

quote: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
rationale: Meets the preferred position: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice (§29.4) with a refund of prepaid fees and no early-termination fee, and Vendor has no convenience right during the term (§9 gives Vendor only breach/insolvency rights).

quote: Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer.
rationale: Preferred position met: once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable via an independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to Customer systems or unrelated data.

quote: This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
rationale: Preferred position met: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County; no arbitration. The pre-suit executive escalation in §28.3 does not delay urgent relief and is unobjectionable.

quote: Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.
rationale: The only MFN runs in Customer's favour (§7.6) and §12.3 confirms Customer has given no most-favoured-customer commitment. This benefits us; no redline.

quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
rationale: Preferred position met: no minimum commitment, take-or-pay or shortfall exposure, and §7.1 bars unstated minimum-use charges. §12.3 reconfirms no minimum-volume commitment.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: There is no non-solicit or no-hire binding Customer anywhere in the document (no "solicit" language at all), and §12.3 expressly disclaims any no-hire commitment. Preferred position met.

quote: Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand.
rationale: Preferred position met: automatic 12-month renewals with a 30-day Customer opt-out, a 60-day Vendor reminder (with deadline extension if missed), and renewal uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

quote: Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form.
rationale: Preferred position met: up to six months of transition assistance at Order Form rates, Customer Data return within 30 days in a machine-readable format (with no fee-dispute hold-back), and certified deletion only after Customer confirms successful return.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
rationale: Meets or exceeds the preferred position: professional/workmanlike services warranty, 90-day Deliverable conformance plus full-term hosted-Services conformance, compliance with law and no-malicious-code warranties, and a re-perform/repair/replace-then-refund remedy (§19.4). The disclaimer in §19.5 expressly does not limit the express warranties.

quote: Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.
rationale: Preferred limits are met in full (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' comp), with certificates on request and confirmation that insurance does not limit Vendor's liability.
